text:
alex: Quick q — how should the API treat the `Accept-Model` header when clients send `Accept-Model: model=redwood-v2; version=42`? Are we treating missing `version` as latest stable or as a tenant default fallback? Trying to spec SDK behavior before I open a PR.

mira: Current behavior (implementation note): if `version` is missing -> use server-side tenant `default_model` (explicit pin). If `Accept-Model` contains `version` -> we honor exact match. If model/version not available we currently return 422. We should standardize fallback ordering: exact version -> compatible minor -> tenant default -> error. Also open question on status code (422 vs 406).

dan: For mobile SDK we prefer deterministic fallback instead of an immediate error. Can SDKs opt into fallback behavior (so older clients that expect 422 still get error)?

mira: We discussed `X-Accept-Fallback` ages ago but never shipped. I don't love adding new headers mid-cycle. My vote: keep server policy-driven and configurable per-customer. Default rollout: `fallback-to-default` for public tenants; allow `strict` flag for enterprise via tenant config.

sasha: PR I opened (https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/5142) proposes `Accept-Model: model=foo; version=...; strict=true` to make it explicit. Is that ok? cc @mira

mira: I'd rather not add boolean flags inside `Accept-Model` (parsing & backward compat risk). If we need explicit strict mode, use `X-Model-Strict: true` or tenant config. But let's minimize header surface area.

alex: For the SDKs we can implement the following pattern: if `Accept-Model` has `version` -> honor it; else use server default. Provide SDK option `on_unsupported` with choices `raise|fallback_to_default|try_compatible` so app owners can opt. That keeps server simpler.

dan: Sounds good. What's our deprecation timeline if we change server default from `error`->`fallback`? Some customers rely on 422 to detect missing models.

mira: We need a deprecation plan: 6 weeks total: 2 weeks announcement, 2 weeks opt-in via experimental header `X-Enable-Fallback`, 2 weeks enforcement. Communication: API changelog + direct emails to tenants >1k monthly tokens + console banner. Add migration guide showing how to set `Accept-Model` and SDK `on_unsupported`.

alex: Can you add that timeline to the API deprecations doc? I'll coordinate comms and legal review.

deploy-bot: canary deployment to eng-runtime using `api:v3-accept-header-fix` started at 2026-03-17T15:12Z :rocket:

sasha: I'll update PR to remove `strict` from `Accept-Model` and instead add `X-Model-Strict` as an enterprise opt-in. Will also patch the API spec at /docs/api/headers.md and include examples.

mira: Tests needed: unit tests for header parsing, integration test for fallback ordering (exact -> compatible minor -> tenant default -> 422), and an end-to-end with dedicated tenant config toggling strict vs fallback.

alex: Action items: (1) Sasha update PR to spec & examples, (2) Mira add deprecation timeline to api-deprecations.md and test plan, (3) Dan add `on_unsupported` option to mobile/web SDKs and a migration example, (4) Alex draft customer comms and coordinate legal. I'll follow up with brief RFC in #eng-platform. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

mira: one more: add logging metric `model.request.fallback` so we can measure impact during canary and ramp-up.

alex: good call — add that to the monitoring checklist.

[thread pinned to #eng-runtime for visibility]
